name: JSN-SR04T waterproof ultrasonic distance sensor
description: Waterproof ultrasonic rangefinder: a sealed 40 kHz probe on a cable plus a small control board. In its default mode (R27 not fitted) it works like an HC-SR04: a TRIG pulse of at least 10 us starts a measurement and ECHO goes high for the sound's round trip (distance = time x 340 m/s / 2, 58.82 us per cm), about 20-600 cm with a 20 cm blind zone; with no echo, ECHO stays high about 38 ms. Runs on 3.0-5.5 V, under 8 mA; ECHO swings to the supply voltage. Sold as: JSN-SR04T-2.0 waterproof ultrasonic module (blue control board, 4-pin header 5V, Trig, Echo, GND, R27 open = mode 1, 2.5 m probe cable).
eli5: A waterproof sound 'eye' on a cable: it chirps too high for you to hear and times how long the echo takes, so your board knows how far away the water or wall is.

pins.name: 5V
pins.description: Supply, 3.0-5.5 V (datasheet). ECHO swings to this voltage, so use 3.3 V on ESP32/Pico or add a divider on ECHO when powered from 5 V

pins.name: Trig
pins.description: Trigger input: a high pulse of at least 10 us starts one measurement (RX in serial modes)

pins.name: Echo
pins.description: Echo output: high for the round-trip time, 58.82 us per cm; about 38 ms if nothing is detected (TX in serial modes)

buildNotes: Leave R27 empty (factory default) for trigger/echo mode; a 47 k resistor there switches to automatic serial output and 120 k to serial on request (0x55).
ECHO is driven to the supply voltage. Power the module from 3.3 V for a direct ESP32/Pico connection, or from 5 V with a divider (e.g. 1 k / 2 k) on ECHO.
Pulse TRIG high for at least 10 us (20 us is more reliable at 3.3 V); distance cm = ECHO high time in us / 58.82.
Wait at least 50-60 ms between measurements. With nothing in range ECHO stays high about 38 ms; treat that as out of range.
Objects closer than about 20-25 cm sit in the blind zone and read wrong. Mount the probe facing straight at a flat target (water surface) with nothing in its 75 degree cone.

driver.code:
# JSN-SR04T-2.0 waterproof ultrasonic distance module, MicroPython driver.
# Mode 1 (factory default, R27 not fitted): trigger/echo pulses.
# Datasheet: hold TRIG high for at least 10 us; the module sends 8 x 40 kHz and
# drives ECHO high for the sound's round trip. distance = high time x 340 m/s / 2,
# i.e. 58.82 us per cm. With no echo, ECHO stays high about 38 ms (and drops by
# 60 ms at the latest). Measure no more often than every 50-60 ms.
from machine import Pin, time_pulse_us
import time

US_PER_CM = 58.82      # 2 / 340 m/s, from the datasheet formula
MIN_CM = 20            # blind zone (datasheet "recent range")
MAX_CM = 600           # datasheet "farthest range"
_MAX_US = 36000        # longer than a 600 cm echo, shorter than the 38 ms no-echo pulse
_CYCLE_MS = 60         # datasheet: cycle period no less than 50 ms; ECHO ends by 60 ms


class JSNSR04T:
    def __init__(self, trig, echo, trigger_us=20):
        # trig / echo: GPIO numbers or Pin objects
        self.trig = trig if isinstance(trig, Pin) else Pin(trig, Pin.OUT, value=0)
        self.trig.init(Pin.OUT, value=0)
        self.echo = echo if isinstance(echo, Pin) else Pin(echo, Pin.IN)
        # 10 us is the datasheet minimum; 20 us is more reliable on 3.3 V supplies
        self.trigger_us = max(10, trigger_us)
        self._last = time.ticks_add(time.ticks_ms(), -_CYCLE_MS)

    def pulse_us(self):
        """Raw ECHO high time in us, or None if no valid echo."""
        wait = _CYCLE_MS - time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), self._last)
        if wait > 0:
            time.sleep_ms(wait)
        self.trig.value(0)
        time.sleep_us(5)
        self.trig.value(1)
        time.sleep_us(self.trigger_us)
        self.trig.value(0)
        self._last = time.ticks_ms()
        t = time_pulse_us(self.echo, 1, 70000)
        if t < 0 or t > _MAX_US:
            return None   # timeout, or the 38 ms "nothing detected" pulse
        return t

    def distance_cm(self):
        """Distance in cm (about 20-600), or None if out of range / no echo."""
        t = self.pulse_us()
        if t is None:
            return None
        return t / US_PER_CM

    def distance_mm(self):
        d = self.distance_cm()
        return None if d is None else int(d * 10 + 0.5)

example.code:
from machine import Pin
import time
from jsnsr04t import JSNSR04T

sensor = JSNSR04T({TRIG}, {ECHO})
while True:
    d = sensor.distance_cm()
    if d is None:
        print('out of range')
    else:
        print('D=%dcm' % round(d))
    time.sleep_ms(200)
